quotes.text: Power Platform isn't four separate apps. It's one connected layer that lets anyone build, automate and analyze without needing a developer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: One-sentence definition that sums up the whole episode.

quotes.text: Most people think Power Platform is only for IT professionals. It isn't. It's designed for anyone in your company, from sales to HR to operations, to create solutions without writing code.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a common misconception about who Power Platform is for.

quotes.text: Power BI is more than just a reporting tool. It's the eyes of the platform. It shows you what's happening across your entire business in real time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable metaphor for the role of Power BI in the platform.

quotes.text: That logic lives inside Dataverse, not inside each individual app. So every app that uses that data follows the same rules.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why centralizing business rules in Dataverse matters.

quotes.text: Most people jump in and try to learn all five tools at once. Don't do that. Instead pick the one tool that solves your biggest pain point today.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, practical recommendation on how to get started.

takeaways: Power Platform is one connected low-code layer on top of Microsoft 365 that combines Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps, Copilot Studio and Dataverse.
Dataverse is the shared data foundation that enforces security, business rules and relationships for every app and flow that uses it.
Start with the single tool that solves your biggest pain point and automate one repetitive process before expanding.
hook: Spreadsheets updated by hand, approvals stuck in email and data copied between disconnected systems slow down almost every organization. This episode explains Microsoft Power Platform in plain English for business users and IT pros alike. You will learn what Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps, Copilot Studio and Dataverse each do and how they snap together into one automated process.
